rows.title: Open problem: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation
rows.body:

rows.title: Attempt on An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation structural argument Result: If a geodesic deviates transversely by n^xi and the norm has quadratic curvature, the deterministic excess norm over a displacement of length n has order n*(n^(xi-1))^2=n^(2xi-1). This yields the proposed balance only after assuming random fluctuations are of the same order. Check: The power follows from norm homogeneity and the square of the relative transverse displacement. A curvature exponent kappa would instead give kappa*xi-(kappa-1). Obstruction: Both the required exponent existence and error control when replacing random passage times by the norm remain unproved for a concrete iid law here. The balance calculation is conditional, not a proof.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0110-an-iid-fpp-law-with-proved-kpz-exponent-relation
No independent review

rows.title: FPP chi=1/3 campaign - CORRECTED 2026-08-22 by lane P3's referee pass; supersedes the 2026-08-15 fire-4 novelty-downgrade row and restates it whole. ONLY ONE PHRASE CHANGED: that row read "(C3) is constant-A doubling hence wall-equivalent". Wall-equivalence is not an exact biconditional - constant-A doubling delivers beta = O(1) through CRUX 9.8's true-ratio route at the blocks the geodesic meets with probability of order one, not at the near-band small-p blocks, and the converse gives the M-fold ratio rather than the 2-fold one. The row's own conclusion is unaffected: (C3) at M = 2 IS verbatim constant-A doubling, so the continuity route's marginal content is TRANSPORT only. THE REST STANDS AS WRITTEN. Quantile interpolation F_t^{-1} := (1-t) F_0^{-1} + t F_1^{-1} between non-degenerate laws on [a,b] stays on [a,b], preserves non-degeneracy and has modulus eta(h) <= h(b-a), so doubling for ONE such law would give Var = O(n^{1-log2/logM}) for EVERY such law. THE NOVELTY CLAIM STAYS DOWNGRADED to new in this specific form, not new in kind, on the declared literature pass: (i) Chatterjee, "The universal relation between scaling exponents in first-passage percolation", Annals of Math 177 (2013), arXiv 1105.4566, proves chi = 2 xi - 1 and states it is universal, independent of dimension and of the weight law under moment assumptions, so distribution-independence of FPP exponents is an established theme; (ii) Damron-Hanson-Sosoe, arXiv 1306.1197 (PTRF), get sublinear variance for general distributions directly under only 2 + log moments, a condition strictly weaker than the bounded support the continuity lemma needs, with no transfer argument at all. The transfer principle is therefore narrower than the state of the art on the axis it trades in. It is not vacuous - the target transferred is the polynomial n^{1-eps} nobody has for any single law - but it must never be presented as a new idea about universality. chi = 1/3 UNMOVED.
